title: Apple Corps settles legal action with Allen Klein’s ABKCO | 1977
content:
Apple Corps ended its legal dispute with Allen Klein’s ABKCO on 8 January 1977.

The legal action stemmed from a lawsuit, filed in the New York Supreme Court by Klein in July 1973, against John Lennon, George Harrison, and Ringo Starr, as well as Apple Records and Apple Films. Klein was seeking to recoup money from loans and advances that Lennon had received during the time of Klein’s management.

In November that year the three former Beatles and Apple Corps countersued, alleging that ABKCO had breached its fiduciary duties. Lennon settled in April 1975, agreeing to pay Klein $135,000 as a final settlement.

The lawsuit against Apple Corps was similarly settled out of court, and finalised on this day. Apple Corps agreed to pay ABKCO $5,009,200 to settle all disputes in the US and UK. ABKCO in turn agreed to pay $800,000, to be divided between Apple Records, Apple Films, Harrisongs, and Ringo Starr, and purchased 52,882 of its common shares from Lennon, Harrison, and Starr.

The agreement was analysed in London’s High Court on 12 January, and both parties agreed that it “disposed of all points at issue”.
